text: { "entries": [ { "name_han": "...", "logic_thesis": "...", "logic_chain": "...", "logic_practice": "...", "logic_compare": "..." } ] }{"entries":[{"name_han":"老子道德经序诀","logic_thesis":"This preface does not merely introduce the Daodejing; it proves that the five-thousand-character text is the operative body of pre-cosmic Dao itself, not a human book. Because Laozi is identified with Dao prior to Heaven and Earth, reciting and embodying the text is not literary study but a causal mechanism that realigns the practitioner with the generative root of cosmos. Efficacy (spirit-response, disaster-extinction, longevity of spirit) follows only when the text is treated as living Dao rather than doctrine.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Laozi is not a Zhou sage who began in history but Dao incarnate, born of Taiwu before heaven-earth and without aging. 2) Inference: What such a being writes cannot be mere counsel; it is the natural scripture (天人自然经) that packages the source of morality and cosmology. 3) Inference: Therefore the 5000 words are both macrocosmic (大无不包) and microcosmic (细无不入). 4) Inference: Rigorous study, stillness, and inner vision cause spirit-response because like resonates with like—mind purified to Dao meets Dao. 5) Conclusion: The text’s power is not magical addition but the recovery of what already is: calamity ceases and spirits submit when the practitioner’s conduct matches Dao’s naturalness. 6) Meta-conclusion: Transmission is for ‘those who have the Dao’; without that prior orientation, the same words remain ink.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi reading: treat chart patterns as local instantiations of the same pre-cosmic order the preface ascribes to Dao—do not moralize stems/branches; map them as natural currents. 2) Daily: short silent recitation of core Daodejing chapters after settling breath, aiming for ‘inner vision of form-shadow’ rather than conceptual grasp. 3) When chart shows clash/void: apply the preface’s sequence—stillness first, then response—before remedial ritual. 4) Teacher-student: only transmit interpretive keys after testing sincerity (法信逻辑), mirroring the text’s restriction to ‘有道者’. 5) Measure progress by reduced reactivity (祸灭/神伏 as calm under affliction), not by mystical experiences.","logic_compare":"Unlike Heshanggong or Xiang’er, which allegorize the Daodejing into longevity techniques or communal ethics, the Xujue argues the text’s ontology: Laozi *is* Dao, so the book *is* the root. It differs from pure philosophical readings by making ritual-contemplative efficacy the proof of metaphysics, and from later neidan commentaries by remaining pre-technical—no furnace language, only jingjin, jing, and neiguan as the causal path."},{"name_han":"太极祭炼内法","logic_thesis":"Zheng Sixiao proves that universal salvation of wandering souls is impossible without the officiant’s own internal refinement: external liturgy is empty form unless yin-yang in the operator’s body is first restored to Dao. The work thus establishes a causal priority—self-alchemy before other-salvation—turning jilian from spectacle into a strict moral-energetic law.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: One yin and one yang is Dao; all beings trapped in form-qi are cut off from Dao. 2) Premise: Hungry ghosts and hell-beings are extreme cases of form-qi blockage. 3) Inference: Rituals that break hell, summon souls, feed, refine, and transmit precepts only work if the operator can generate pure yang from within. 4) Inference: Therefore ‘internal method’ is not optional ornament but the engine of ‘external rite’. 5) Conclusion: Simplified jilian as an independent rite still depends on the same inner law; without it, food and talismans do not liberate. 6) Ethical conclusion: Compassion without self-refinement is structurally false.","logic_practice":"1) Before any ancestor/ghost work timed by BaZi death-day or 7th-month cycles: complete a personal quieting and yang-raising practice (breath, stillness, heart purity). 2) Map the deceased’s chart for cold-damp or weak fire patterns; design jilian timing on days that support the officiant’s yang, not only the calendar festival. 3) Use the text’s sequence as checklist: break obstruction → call → feed → refine → precept → send; never skip refine for spectacle. 4) After ritual, audit own body-mind state; if depleted, the method was externalized wrongly. 5) Teach clients that ‘helping the dead’ begins with regulating one’s own five phases.","logic_compare":"Unlike standard Lingbao shidu liturgies that emphasize scriptural power and multi-stage public ceremony, this text collapses the chain into a portable rite whose authority is the operator’s neifa. It differs from pure neidan manuals by keeping other-salvation as the telos, and from purely moral Buddhist feeding rites by insisting on Daoist yin-yang physiology as the causal medium."},{"name_han":"金石簿","logic_thesis":"This work proves that mineral and metal substances are not arbitrary materia but graded carriers of celestial qi whose correct identification, pairing, and fire-timing constitute a reproducible path from gross matter to refined elixir. Its logic is taxonomic and experimental: without precise knowledge of stone-metal natures, external alchemy collapses into poison or waste.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Heaven’s qi condenses into stones and metals with distinct virtues. 2) Premise: Human body can assimilate those virtues if toxicity and timing are mastered. 3) Inference: Cataloguing names, qualities, companions, and taboos is epistemic duty, not trivia. 4) Inference: Wrong sequence or impure material inverts the intended transformation (illness, death). 5) Conclusion: Successful waidan is applied natural philosophy: matching substance to phase and fire to season. 6) Methodological conclusion: Record and verify—tradition without testing is unreliable.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi-informed health counsel: map mineral remedies only after reading the native’s phase excess/deficiency (e.g., strong water + cold metal may contraindicate certain heavy cold minerals). 2) Treat ‘fire phases’ in lab analogy as life-stage timing: do not force intense refinement on charts already in death/grave phases without support. 3) For cultivation: prefer internal analogues (saliva, breath, light) over literal toxic metals unless under historical-scholarly, non-ingestion study. 4) Practice precise naming—confusing cinnabar grades is the symbolic equivalent of misreading a Day Master. 5) Keep a verification log: any ‘remedy’ must show measurable balance change, not faith claim.","logic_compare":"Unlike theoretical Taiqing danjing that stress mythic origins and divine transmission, Jinshi Bu is inventory-logic: what each substance *does*. It differs from medical bencao by orienting every entry toward elixir transformation rather than disease alone, and from neidan texts that reject minerals by still affirming matter as teachable qi rather than pure metaphor."},{"name_han":"太清五髓经","logic_thesis":"The scripture argues that longevity is secured by concentrating and circulating five ‘marrows’ (essential fluids/qi corresponding to the five organs and five phases) until they fuse into a pure Taiqing substrate. It proves cultivation as reconstitution of microcosmic five-phase marrow, not mere moral purity or outer drugs alone.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Life depends on five organ essences (marrows) that mirror five phases. 2) Premise: Dissipation of marrow is the causal path of aging and disease. 3) Inference: Techniques that close leakage and return essence upward reverse the causal path. 4) Inference: When five marrows cohere, the body approximates Taiqing purity. 5) Conclusion: Immortality discourse here is physiological coherence of five essences. 6) Practical conclusion: Order of work must follow phase generation/control, not random exercises.","logic_practice":"1) BaZi: identify which organ-phase is chronically over-leaking (e.g., wood Day Master with multiple output stems → liver/blood-marrow care). 2) Design daily practice around the weakest marrow first, then generating cycle support. 3) Seasonal timing: harvest and store essence in corresponding wang seasons; avoid forceful practice in phase death. 4) Pair breath retention / quiet sitting with dietary phase balance rather than extreme austerity. 5) Success metric: stable sleep, less involuntary loss, even emotional tone across five phases.","logic_compare":"Compared with Huangting’s poetic visceral spirits, Wusui Jing is more marrow-essence engineering. It differs from pure jing-qi-shen neidan ladders by centering five parallel essences rather than a single sequential refinement, and from waidan Taiqing texts by locating the ‘Taiqing’ product inside bodily fluids rather than the crucible."},{"name_han":"太上正一盟威朝仪","logic_thesis":"This text proves that legitimate spiritual authority in Zhengyi Daoism is contractual: only through covenantal petition, ranked audience, and correct court protocol does the human officer interface with celestial offices. Ritual form is not pageantry; it is the legal grammar that makes petitions binding in the spirit-bureaucracy.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Cosmos is administered by ranked officials under Dao’s mandate (盟威). 2) Premise: Humans may participate only by oath, register, and ritual office. 3) Inference: Morning audience (朝) reenacts correct hierarchy—disorder of form = disorder of mandate. 4) Inference: Without covenant, talismans and petitions lack standing (no ‘jurisdiction’). 5) Conclusion: Efficacy of Zhengyi practice tracks ritual-legal correctness plus moral keeping of the oath. 6) Social conclusion: Community order mirrors celestial court order.","logic_practice":"1) For BaZi remediation via Zhengyi-style petition: write clear ‘case file’—stem/branch affliction as charge, requested rectification as judgment sought. 2) Time audiences on days when the native’s useful god is strong and officer-star (official/7k) is not wildly hostile without support. 3) Maintain personal ‘covenant hygiene’: no petition while knowingly violating core precepts you already accepted. 4) Structure prayer as court document: title, identity, facts, request, closing formula—not emotional venting. 5) After rite, act in worldly law/ethics consistently; contradiction voids the symbolic contract.","logic_compare":"Unlike Lingbao cosmogonic liturgies focused on universal salvation scripts, Zhengyi chaoyi is bureaucratic-legal. It differs from Shangqing’s visionary ascent (where the adept sees and merges) by emphasizing petition through office and oath. Compared with folk free-form prayer, it insists that form *is* the power channel."},{"name_han":"太上说豁落七元经","logic_thesis":"The text proves that mortality crises, epidemics, and demonic harassment are administrative and stellar: the Northern Emperor and Seven Yuan control life-death registers, so unblocking, lamp-ritual, and invocation of the seven luminaries can rewrite misfortune at the level of cosmic registry, not only psychology.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Northern realm and Seven Yuan oversee ghosts and human lifespan books. 2) Premise: Calamity is often register-blockage or malefic stellar-demonic influence. 3) Inference: Aligning with Seven Yuan (recitation, lamps, talismans, memorials) petitions the competent court. 4) Inference: Multi-day focused practice concentrates intent enough to ‘move the register’. 5) Conclusion: Deliverance is jurisdictional appeal, not generic piety. 6) Cautionary conclusion: Only sincere, law-abiding appeal is honored; magic without virtue fails.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi: when chart shows heavy 七杀/羊刃/空亡 clusters with illness stars, consider Seven Yuan / Beidou-type timing rather than only five-element objects. 2) Lamp practice on days ruled by the afflicted planet/phase for that native. 3) Combine medical care with ritual—registry logic does not cancel physical cause. 4) Use 1×7 or 2×7 day intensive recitation windows when luck pillar enters clash. 5) Frame intent as ‘correct the book’, not hatred of enemies.","logic_compare":"Unlike general xiaomo (demon-dissolving) scriptures that stress wisdom-power of the adept, this text localizes authority in Beidi and Seven Yuan as officers of death-files. It differs from pure astrology by adding petitionary rite, and from pure exorcism by tying results to lifespan calculation (益算/解厄) rather than only expulsion."},{"name_han":"灵宝施食科仪","logic_thesis":"Lingbao food-offering liturgy proves that postmortem suffering is partly hunger of unrefined qi, and that correctly empowered food, mantra, and mudra can convert that hunger into liberation. The argument is sacramental causality: ordinary food does not feed ghosts; transformed food does, because the rite changes the ontological status of the offering.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Wandering souls suffer lack—food, light, precepts, direction. 2) Premise: Lingbao methods can ‘open throat’, multiply food, and refine qi. 3) Inference: Without transformation mantras, offering remains human nutrition only. 4) Inference: Sequence (invite, purify, empower, distribute, dedicate, send) is the causal machine. 5) Conclusion: Compassion becomes effective when ritual technology matches the beings’ mode of existence. 6) Communal conclusion: Feeding the dead reorders the living community’s debt and fear.","logic_practice":"1) Schedule施食 near death-anniversary stems/branches or Zhongyuan, checking that officiant’s chart can support water-fire balance that day. 2) Before offering, regulate breath and intention so ‘empowerment’ is not empty chant. 3) Name categories of beings (ancestors, lonely souls, disaster dead) to avoid vague magic. 4) Dedicate merit back to the living chart’s useful gods—close the loop. 5) Teach families that ethical amends in life reduce the ‘hunger’ their dead carry.","logic_compare":"Unlike Buddhist Yankou, which is its sibling in form, Lingbao shishi embeds Daoist salvation ranks, talismans, and Heavenly Worthies as the conversion engine. It differs from Zhengyi court petitions (legal) by being alimentary-transformative, and from jilian neifa by remaining more liturgical-public than operator-alchemy centered."},{"name_han":"历世真仙体道通鉴后编","logic_thesis":"The sequel-hagiography proves Dao by induction across history: successive verified biographies of embodied immortals show that ‘attaining Dao’ is a repeatable human possibility, not a mythic singularity. Its logic is evidentiary—pattern of lives, methods, and outcomes constitutes a collective proof stronger than any single claim.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: If Dao were unreal, consistent long-term cases of transformation would not accumulate. 2) Premise: Multiple eras and methods still converge on embodiment (体道). 3) Inference: Diversity of paths is compatible with unity of goal. 4) Inference: Failures and partial attainments in the record refine what counts as evidence. 5) Conclusion: Hagiography is a dataset for cultivating confidence and method selection. 6) Meta-conclusion: Later generations inherit a duty to continue the empirical-spiritual ledger.","logic_practice":"1) When a BaZi shows strong ‘immortal’ patterns (clear output + resource + seal with stable structure), study matching historical cases rather than generic advice. 2) Extract method families from biographies (alchemy, ritual, virtue, hermit) and match to chart temperament. 3) Use ‘通鉴’ attitude: track your own practice years as data, not drama. 4) Avoid single-guru absolutism—the corpus itself is plural. 5) Treat moral biography (deeds) as seriously as technique chapters.","logic_compare":"Unlike doctrinal scriptures that argue from cosmology downward, this work argues from cases upward. It differs from pure genealogies of gods by focusing on human practitioners across dynasties, and from technical manuals by subordinating recipe detail to the narrative proof that embodiment happened."},{"name_han":"太清阴阳五行经","logic_thesis":"This classic proves that all fortune, body, and practice outcomes are functions of yin-yang imbalance and five-phase generation/control cycles operating uniformly from cosmos to person. It establishes the shared algebraic grammar underlying medicine, alchemy, and fate calculation—without which BaZi would be superstition and cultivation would be random.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Dao differentiates as yin-yang. 2) Premise: Yin-yang further articulates as five phases with fixed generation and conquest relations. 3) Inference: Any concrete system (organs, seasons, stems, branches, medicines) is a mapping onto this algebra. 4) Inference: Diagnosis is locating excess/deficiency and blocked cycles. 5) Conclusion: Remedy is restoring dynamic balance, not maximizing one phase. 6) Universal conclusion: Taiqing purity is balanced five-phase circulation, not annihilation of yin.","logic_practice":"1) Standard BaZi workflow: Day Master strength → useful god → taboo god, always justified in generation/control language. 2) For annual luck: check whether incoming pillar generates useful god or strengthens taboo. 3) Cultivation: time breathing/meditation to support deficient phases (e.g., more restorative practice in seasons that feed the weak phase). 4) Refuse one-sided ‘boost metal’ style fixes when control cycle will rebound. 5) Cross-check body symptoms with phase theory before spiritualizing problems.","logic_compare":"Compared with pure Yijing image-number, this text is more explicitly five-phase medical-alchemical. It differs from moral Daodejing readings by being operational cosmology, and from star-lore (Seven Yuan) by grounding causality in elemental relations rather than stellar officers."},{"name_han":"黄帝太一八门逆顺生死诀","logic_thesis":"The text proves that life-death outcomes in movement, combat, and selection of time-space are governed by Taiyi’s eight gates running in reverse or forward according to yin-yang dun patterns. Correct alignment with gate-qi can convert a deadly configuration into a viable path; misalignment inverts luck even on a ‘good’ calendar day.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Taiyi cycles and eight gates (休生伤杜景死惊开) structure spatial-temporal luck. 2) Premise: Yang-dun and yin-dun reverse the running of stems vs gates. 3) Inference: ‘生/开/休’ gates favor life and entry; ‘死/伤/惊’ favor avoidance or attack under rule. 4) Inference: Formulae that place 戊 on 休 and run gates/stems correctly yield ‘immortal path not far’. 5) Conclusion: Survival strategy is navigational knowledge of reverse/forward gate-law. 6) Extension: The same logic applies to choosing dwellings, travel, and ritual timing.","logic_practice":"1) When BaZi year/month is harsh, select event days where local 奇门/太乙 gate supporting the native’s useful god is open (生/开/休). 2) Avoid signing, surgery, or confrontation on personal 死/惊 gates unless the method specifically uses them. 3) For exorcistic or assertive rites, prefer gates that match intent (e.g., 伤 for cutting, 开 for initiating). 4) Learn yang-dun vs yin-dun half-year switch so you do not run formulae backward. 5) Integrate with BaZi: gate choice is tactical; chart structure is strategic.","logic_compare":"Unlike BaZi, which profiles a life’s phase economy from birth data, this text is operational time-space tactics under Taiyi. It differs from pure Liuren or standard Qimen manuals mainly in its explicit ‘逆顺生死’ framing and legendary military transmission, emphasizing survival polarity over general divination breadth."},{"name_han":"上清太极隐注玉经宝诀","logic_thesis":"This Shangqing-Lingbao hybrid proves that scriptures are graded living forces: correct reception, collation, and recitation under oath determine whether texts heal and immortalize or inflict ‘wind-blade’ penalties. Transmission protocol is the safety lock on cosmic software; hidden annotations reveal that method without ritual legality backfires.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Jade scriptures are high-frequency true writs, not ordinary books. 2) Premise: Errors in characters, illicit transmission, or impure reception injure lifespan. 3) Inference: Collation thrice, pure covenants, and graded eligibility protect both parties. 4) Inference: Recitation of proper texts can offset karmic disease when done under ritual frame. 5) Conclusion: Spiritual literacy is regulated access to power, analogous to handling medicine. 6) Soteriological conclusion: Seeing this text marks predestined immortal office—if vows are kept.","logic_practice":"1) Treat any advanced BaZi/Daoist formula set as ‘经’: document lineage of method, do not remix casually. 2) Before teaching a powerful remedial rite, require a period of purity and clear vows (no harm, no sale of fear). 3) When clients have chronic unexplained illness in chart, combine medical care with ordered scripture-recitation rather than random mantras. 4) Maintain textual hygiene—wrong strokes in talismans are the modern equivalent of wrong characters. 5) Prefer fewer authentic practices over many leaked fragments.","logic_compare":"Unlike public Daodejing prefaces that invite broad cultivation, this text restricts and weaponizes access. It differs from Zhengyi court codes by focusing on scripture-as-body and visionary Shangqing grades, and from pure morality precepts by making philological care (字校) itself a salvific discipline."},{"name_han":"太上灵宝胞胎经","logic_thesis":"The scripture proves that advanced attainment recreates the embryonic state: by returning breath, spirit, and intention to the ‘womb’ of the body-cosmos, the adept restarts generation from the undivided, escaping the exhaustion of postnatal qi. Embryonic breathing is not metaphor alone but the causal reset of life-process.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Postnatal life leaks original qi through breath, emotion, and desire. 2) Premise: The fetus lives without ordinary panting, nourished by primordial unity. 3) Inference: Practices that close the mouth-nose dependence and interiorize breath reverse leakage. 4) Inference: When spirit rests in the lower/central ‘womb’, postnatal and prenatal reconnect. 5) Conclusion: Longevity and spiritual rebirth share one mechanism—embryonic return. 6) Warning: Forced breath-holding without guidance inverts the benefit.","logic_practice":"1) For BaZi charts with severe rootlessness or exhausted resource, prioritize soft embryonic breathing over intense cathartic practices. 2) Practice after midnight or in quiet hours when postnatal stimulation is low. 3) Couple with moral quietude—anger and lust are anti-embryonic. 4) Use seasonal ‘storage’ months to deepen, not to push extremes. 5) Track pulse, sleep, and emotional reactivity as indicators of true return vs repression.","logic_compare":"Compared with general qi-absorption methods, Baotai Jing specifies the fetal model as the gold standard of breath. It differs from sexual-alchemy dual cultivation by being primarily solitary-interior, and from waidan by locating the womb of rebirth in the practitioner’s own psychosomatic field."},{"name_han":"太上说消魔经","logic_thesis":"This text proves that ‘demons’ are both external pathogens and internal afflictive forces, and that they dissolve under clarified wisdom-power and correct recitation rather than under mere violence. The core argument: obstruction is removable because it lacks ultimate root in Dao; illumination cancels it.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Demonic interference thrives on fear, turbidity, and ignorance. 2) Premise: Dao’s true writ carries clarifying force (消). 3) Inference: Recitation plus upright mind removes fuel demons need. 4) Inference: Internal demons (三尸-type passions) and external specters share a vulnerability to clarity. 5) Conclusion: Exorcism without self-purification is incomplete; self-purification is already half exorcism. 6) Pastoral conclusion: Teach courage and clarity as primary talismans.","logic_practice":"1) When BaZi shows heavy sha and illness with panic symptoms, combine boundary-setting rites with cognitive-clarity practice (name the fear precisely). 2) Daily short recitation aimed at ‘dissolving turbidity’, not cursing enemies. 3) Clean sleep, diet, and media inputs—turbid lifestyle feeds ‘魔’. 4) Use days when seal/resource stars support the native for formal 消魔 work. 5) Evaluate success by reduced compulsion and clearer decisions, not only omens.","logic_compare":"Unlike Seven Yuan / Beidi texts that appeal to stellar-northern jurisdiction, Xiaomo Jing emphasizes the dissolving power of revealed wisdom itself. It differs from purely medical pathogen theory by retaining moral-spiritual agency, and from jilian by targeting affliction of the living more than salvation of the dead."},{"name_han":"太上说西王母益算经","logic_thesis":"The scripture proves lifespan is numerically administered (‘算’) and can be increased through alliance with Xiwangmu’s life-bestowing authority when the petitioner meets moral and ritual conditions. It establishes that years are not only biological residue but adjustable allotment under divine accounting.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Each person has a lifespan count overseen by celestial offices, with Xiwangmu as a paramount life-nourishing figure. 2) Premise: Misdeeds and ritual neglect shorten count; virtue and proper petition can restore or add. 3) Inference: ‘益算’ rites are accounting corrections, not defiance of Dao. 4) Inference: Efficacy requires sincerity, purity, and correct timing/invocation. 5) Conclusion: Longevity practice includes ethical capital plus formal appeal to the life-giver. 6) Limit: Gains without reformed conduct are unstable.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi, when life-palace and health stars are weak but resources can be cultivated, use 益算 framing for long-horizon lifestyle reform, not panic magic. 2) Birthday or renri rites dedicated to life-extension with concrete vows (quit a vice, serve parents). 3) Pair with medical checkups—算 includes body maintenance. 4) Prefer generating-cycle years for major life-extension retreats. 5) Record baseline health metrics; ‘added years’ should appear as added resilience.","logic_compare":"Compared with general Beidou destiny scriptures, this text privileges Xiwangmu as the life-augmenting pole. It differs from pure neidan longevity (which stores essence) by stressing petitionary increase of the register, and from fatalistic BaZi readings by asserting lawful plasticity of the lifespan number."},{"name_han":"谷神篇","logic_thesis":"Building on Laozi’s ‘Valley Spirit does not die’, this work proves that immortality is the continuous functioning of empty, receptive, generative capacity (玄牝) rather than accumulation of force. The valley is not weak; its emptiness is the indestructible root that births heaven-earth in the body.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: What is full breaks; what is empty can receive without end. 2) Premise: The ‘valley spirit’ names the undying generative emptiness (玄牝之门). 3) Inference: Cultivation that fills the mind with striving kills the valley; yielding preserves it. 4) Inference: Soft continuous use (‘绵绵若存’) outperforms violent effort. 5) Conclusion: True yang is born from protected emptiness, not from aggressive yang-forcing. 6) Neidan conclusion: Guard the mysterious female gate as the practical root of returned elixir.","logic_practice":"1) For charts overloaded with output and officer (busy, drained types): prescribe valley practice—more silence, less performing. 2) Meditation: rest attention in lower belly/empty center without squeezing breath. 3) Speech discipline: reduce unnecessary words as ‘not exhausting the valley’. 4) In yearly luck of extreme fire/wood arousal, deliberately schedule emptiness days. 5) Judge practice by spontaneous stability and less craving, not by dramatic qi sensations.","logic_compare":"Unlike furnace-heavy neidan tracts, Gushen Pian keeps Laozi’s emptiness as the master key. It differs from precept texts (external restraint) by offering an ontological image for why restraint works, and from five-phase engineering texts by prioritizing one metaphor—the living valley—over multi-organ taxonomy."},{"name_han":"还丹众仙论","logic_thesis":"This treatise proves returned-elixir attainment by a chorus of immortal authorities: when many realized figures converge on the same alchemical logic, the method is validated beyond private opinion. The argument is consensus-of-the-realized plus technical unity—many voices, one dan-path.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Isolated claims of immortality are epistemically weak. 2) Premise: Multiple immortals articulate compatible stages of lead-mercury / yin-yang return. 3) Inference: Convergence indicates structure of reality, not sect fashion. 4) Inference: Divergent outer images still point to one reverse-flow of essence-qi-spirit. 5) Conclusion: Study should extract the shared skeleton, discard ornamental contradictions. 6) Practical conclusion: Choose a coherent lineage thread and complete it, using the ‘众仙’ as cross-check.","logic_practice":"1) When reading many masters confuses a student, force a one-page synthesis of shared stages (stop leak → gather → cook → return → stabilize). 2) Match stage emphasis to BaZi: leaky charts start at sealing; stagnant charts at gentle movement. 3) Use biographies inside the text as pacing models—years, not weeks. 4) Reject any modern promise that skips the shared skeleton. 5) Quarterly review: which stage am I actually in, evidenced by life conduct?","logic_compare":"Unlike single-author neidan revelations, this work’s authority is anthological. It differs from hagiography (体道通鉴) by focusing on method-arguments rather than life stories alone, and from purely laboratory waidan by reading ‘returned cinnabar’ primarily as internal reversion illustrated through immortal discourse."},{"name_han":"玄宗直指万法同归","logic_thesis":"Mu Changchao proves that the proliferation of teachings, rites, and phenomena all issue from and return to one mysterious source (玄/元始三炁); therefore sectarian multiplicity is pedagogic, not ultimate. Direct pointing means collapsing ten thousand methods into their single root without nihilism—forms remain useful until return is complete.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Yuanqi differentiates into heaven-earth, three lights, five phases, eight trigrams, humans. 2) Premise: All later dharmas are elaborations of that differentiation. 3) Inference: Clinging to branch methods as absolute multiplies delusion. 4) Inference: Yet denying methods before realizing the root is also error. 5) Conclusion: True mastery uses methods as fingers, then rests in the moon of unified return. 6) Pedagogical conclusion: ‘直指’ is ruthlessly simple orientation amid Daoist scholastic complexity.","logic_practice":"1) For advanced students drowning in techniques: inventory all practices → map each to a root function (quiet, circulate, refine, save beings) → cut redundancies. 2) BaZi counseling: many remedial gadgets → one structural useful-god strategy. 3) Daily: begin and end with a minute of returning attention to source-breath before any complex method. 4) Interfaith/inter-sect reading: translate foreign terms into your root model rather than collecting exoticisms. 5) Success: fewer practices, deeper consistency.","logic_compare":"Compared with early revealed scriptures that multiply heavens and names, this Yuan-Ming synthesis recenters unity. It differs from Chan-style ‘direct pointing’ by keeping Daoist cosmogony (三炁) as the explicit ground, and from purely practical neidan by philosophically justifying why all methods can be collapsed."},{"name_han":"老子节解","logic_thesis":"Sectional exegesis proves that the Daodejing’s power is unlocked only when each pericope is decoded into concrete cultivation or cosmic correspondences rather than left as vague wisdom. The argument: structure of the text is instructional sequence; cutting and explaining sections reveals operative steps hidden in plain language.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Classic speech is compressed and polyvalent. 2) Premise: Without sectional keys, readers moralize or aestheticize without transformation. 3) Inference: Dividing the text into units allows mapping to body, state, and practice. 4) Inference: Early esoteric readings treat political language as inner governance. 5) Conclusion: Correct commentary is a causal interface between scripture and embodiment. 6) Critical conclusion: Commentary must serve practice verification, not literary display.","logic_practice":"1) Study one short section per week; extract one behavioral experiment (e.g., ‘不争’ in a real conflict). 2) Link sections to BaZi themes: humility sections for strong officer charts; contentment for wealth-heavy charts. 3) Keep a dual column: ‘surface meaning’ vs ‘body-state meaning’. 4) Recite only after sectional understanding to avoid empty chanting. 5) Discard interpretations that cannot change a measurable habit in 30 days.","logic_compare":"Unlike the Xujue, which sacralizes the whole text’s ontology, Jie Jie works microscopically on segments. It differs from Heshanggong’s systematic longevity allegory mainly in form (sectional cuts) and from pure philology by insisting that the cut exists for praxis, not for academic completeness alone."},{"name_han":"灵棋经","logic_thesis":"The Lingqi system proves that a simplified, castable image-set can carry Yijing-class decision guidance for ordinary people: because the cosmos’s pattern is ubiquitous, twelve spirit-tokens can sample it when ritual sincerity is present. Accessibility does not cancel depth; it democratizes pattern-reading under constraint of proper making and invocation.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Zhouyi is true but hard for daily use. 2) Premise: Sages may encode the same order in alternative lots (chess-like tokens). 3) Inference: Structured random cast + fixed oracle text yields actionable hexagram-like counsel. 4) Inference: Consecrated implements and prayer align the cast with the questioner’s qi field. 5) Conclusion: Divination works as patterned sampling of a lawful cosmos, not as chaos or fraud. 6) Ethical conclusion: Ask only proper questions; the tool amplifies clarity or confusion already present.","logic_practice":"1) Use Lingqi when BaZi shows a fork (two plausible useful-god strategies) and a timely decision is needed. 2) Cast after stating one precise question; refuse multi-question noise. 3) Interpret oracle lines through the querent’s chart language (phases, official/wealth) for integration. 4) Prefer days when the querent’s seal/resource is not crushed—clarity needs support. 5) Archive casts vs outcomes to calibrate personal accuracy and humility.","logic_compare":"Unlike full Yijing professional yarrow practice, Lingqi is deliberately portable and popular. It differs from Taiyi Eight Gates (time-space tactics for movement/war) by being textual-oracular counsel for civil decisions, and from pure spirit-medium possession by using fixed classical responses rather than open channeling."},{"name_han":"三洞众戒文","logic_thesis":"The collected precepts prove that graded moral-ritual restraints are the load-bearing structure of the Three Caverns path: without precepts, scriptures and techniques lack a vessel and turn destructive. Precepts are not lower than alchemy; they are the causal precondition that makes higher methods non-lethal to self and community.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Three Caverns transmit escalating sacred powers. 2) Premise: Power without restraint multiplies harm (to body, ghosts, society). 3) Inference: Ordination stages bind the adept to corresponding 戒. 4) Inference: Keeping precepts purifies the vessel so qi and spirit can stably rise. 5) Conclusion: Ethical law is technical infrastructure of immortality, not mere social etiquette. 6) Communal conclusion: Shared precepts create a trustworthy field for collective rites.","logic_practice":"1) Before advanced BaZi remediation or ritual work, adopt a minimal personal code (no fraud, no sexual exploitation of clients, no fear-selling). 2) Match precept intensity to method intensity—stronger talismanic work, stricter purity windows. 3) Use confession/repair when broken: precept logic includes restoration, not only perfection. 4) In yearly luck of peer/rob-wealth stress, double down on non-greed precepts. 5) Teach students precepts as success conditions for practice, not as optional piety.","logic_compare":"Unlike pure wisdom texts that dissolve rules after awakening, Sandong precept literature insists rules remain the chassis of transmission. It differs from single-lineage house rules by claiming pan-cavern scope, and from purely civil Confucian ethics by tying each restraint to liturgical eligibility and cosmic consequence."}]}

entries.logic_thesis: This preface does not merely introduce the Daodejing; it proves that the five-thousand-character text is the operative body of pre-cosmic Dao itself, not a human book. Because Laozi is identified with Dao prior to Heaven and Earth, reciting and embodying the text is not literary study but a causal mechanism that realigns the practitioner with the generative root of cosmos. Efficacy (spirit-response, disaster-extinction, longevity of spirit) follows only when the text is treated as living Dao rather than doctrine.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Laozi is not a Zhou sage who began in history but Dao incarnate, born of Taiwu before heaven-earth and without aging. 2) Inference: What such a being writes cannot be mere counsel; it is the natural scripture (天人自然经) that packages the source of morality and cosmology. 3) Inference: Therefore the 5000 words are both macrocosmic (大无不包) and microcosmic (细无不入). 4) Inference: Rigorous study, stillness, and inner vision cause spirit-response because like resonates with like—mind purified to Dao meets Dao. 5) Conclusion: The text’s power is not magical addition but the recovery of what already is: calamity ceases and spirits submit when the practitioner’s conduct matches Dao’s naturalness. 6) Meta-conclusion: Transmission is for ‘those who have the Dao’; without that prior orientation, the same words remain ink.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi reading: treat chart patterns as local instantiations of the same pre-cosmic order the preface ascribes to Dao—do not moralize stems/branches; map them as natural currents. 2) Daily: short silent recitation of core Daodejing chapters after settling breath, aiming for ‘inner vision of form-shadow’ rather than conceptual grasp. 3) When chart shows clash/void: apply the preface’s sequence—stillness first, then response—before remedial ritual. 4) Teacher-student: only transmit interpretive keys after testing sincerity (法信逻辑), mirroring the text’s restriction to ‘有道者’. 5) Measure progress by reduced reactivity (祸灭/神伏 as calm under affliction), not by mystical experiences.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Heshanggong or Xiang’er, which allegorize the Daodejing into longevity techniques or communal ethics, the Xujue argues the text’s ontology: Laozi *is* Dao, so the book *is* the root. It differs from pure philosophical readings by making ritual-contemplative efficacy the proof of metaphysics, and from later neidan commentaries by remaining pre-technical—no furnace language, only jingjin, jing, and neiguan as the causal path.

entries.logic_thesis: Zheng Sixiao proves that universal salvation of wandering souls is impossible without the officiant’s own internal refinement: external liturgy is empty form unless yin-yang in the operator’s body is first restored to Dao. The work thus establishes a causal priority—self-alchemy before other-salvation—turning jilian from spectacle into a strict moral-energetic law.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: One yin and one yang is Dao; all beings trapped in form-qi are cut off from Dao. 2) Premise: Hungry ghosts and hell-beings are extreme cases of form-qi blockage. 3) Inference: Rituals that break hell, summon souls, feed, refine, and transmit precepts only work if the operator can generate pure yang from within. 4) Inference: Therefore ‘internal method’ is not optional ornament but the engine of ‘external rite’. 5) Conclusion: Simplified jilian as an independent rite still depends on the same inner law; without it, food and talismans do not liberate. 6) Ethical conclusion: Compassion without self-refinement is structurally false.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Before any ancestor/ghost work timed by BaZi death-day or 7th-month cycles: complete a personal quieting and yang-raising practice (breath, stillness, heart purity). 2) Map the deceased’s chart for cold-damp or weak fire patterns; design jilian timing on days that support the officiant’s yang, not only the calendar festival. 3) Use the text’s sequence as checklist: break obstruction → call → feed → refine → precept → send; never skip refine for spectacle. 4) After ritual, audit own body-mind state; if depleted, the method was externalized wrongly. 5) Teach clients that ‘helping the dead’ begins with regulating one’s own five phases.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike standard Lingbao shidu liturgies that emphasize scriptural power and multi-stage public ceremony, this text collapses the chain into a portable rite whose authority is the operator’s neifa. It differs from pure neidan manuals by keeping other-salvation as the telos, and from purely moral Buddhist feeding rites by insisting on Daoist yin-yang physiology as the causal medium.

entries.logic_thesis: This work proves that mineral and metal substances are not arbitrary materia but graded carriers of celestial qi whose correct identification, pairing, and fire-timing constitute a reproducible path from gross matter to refined elixir. Its logic is taxonomic and experimental: without precise knowledge of stone-metal natures, external alchemy collapses into poison or waste.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Heaven’s qi condenses into stones and metals with distinct virtues. 2) Premise: Human body can assimilate those virtues if toxicity and timing are mastered. 3) Inference: Cataloguing names, qualities, companions, and taboos is epistemic duty, not trivia. 4) Inference: Wrong sequence or impure material inverts the intended transformation (illness, death). 5) Conclusion: Successful waidan is applied natural philosophy: matching substance to phase and fire to season. 6) Methodological conclusion: Record and verify—tradition without testing is unreliable.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi-informed health counsel: map mineral remedies only after reading the native’s phase excess/deficiency (e.g., strong water + cold metal may contraindicate certain heavy cold minerals). 2) Treat ‘fire phases’ in lab analogy as life-stage timing: do not force intense refinement on charts already in death/grave phases without support. 3) For cultivation: prefer internal analogues (saliva, breath, light) over literal toxic metals unless under historical-scholarly, non-ingestion study. 4) Practice precise naming—confusing cinnabar grades is the symbolic equivalent of misreading a Day Master. 5) Keep a verification log: any ‘remedy’ must show measurable balance change, not faith claim.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike theoretical Taiqing danjing that stress mythic origins and divine transmission, Jinshi Bu is inventory-logic: what each substance *does*. It differs from medical bencao by orienting every entry toward elixir transformation rather than disease alone, and from neidan texts that reject minerals by still affirming matter as teachable qi rather than pure metaphor.

entries.logic_thesis: The scripture argues that longevity is secured by concentrating and circulating five ‘marrows’ (essential fluids/qi corresponding to the five organs and five phases) until they fuse into a pure Taiqing substrate. It proves cultivation as reconstitution of microcosmic five-phase marrow, not mere moral purity or outer drugs alone.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Life depends on five organ essences (marrows) that mirror five phases. 2) Premise: Dissipation of marrow is the causal path of aging and disease. 3) Inference: Techniques that close leakage and return essence upward reverse the causal path. 4) Inference: When five marrows cohere, the body approximates Taiqing purity. 5) Conclusion: Immortality discourse here is physiological coherence of five essences. 6) Practical conclusion: Order of work must follow phase generation/control, not random exercises.
entries.logic_practice: 1) BaZi: identify which organ-phase is chronically over-leaking (e.g., wood Day Master with multiple output stems → liver/blood-marrow care). 2) Design daily practice around the weakest marrow first, then generating cycle support. 3) Seasonal timing: harvest and store essence in corresponding wang seasons; avoid forceful practice in phase death. 4) Pair breath retention / quiet sitting with dietary phase balance rather than extreme austerity. 5) Success metric: stable sleep, less involuntary loss, even emotional tone across five phases.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with Huangting’s poetic visceral spirits, Wusui Jing is more marrow-essence engineering. It differs from pure jing-qi-shen neidan ladders by centering five parallel essences rather than a single sequential refinement, and from waidan Taiqing texts by locating the ‘Taiqing’ product inside bodily fluids rather than the crucible.

entries.logic_thesis: This text proves that legitimate spiritual authority in Zhengyi Daoism is contractual: only through covenantal petition, ranked audience, and correct court protocol does the human officer interface with celestial offices. Ritual form is not pageantry; it is the legal grammar that makes petitions binding in the spirit-bureaucracy.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Cosmos is administered by ranked officials under Dao’s mandate (盟威). 2) Premise: Humans may participate only by oath, register, and ritual office. 3) Inference: Morning audience (朝) reenacts correct hierarchy—disorder of form = disorder of mandate. 4) Inference: Without covenant, talismans and petitions lack standing (no ‘jurisdiction’). 5) Conclusion: Efficacy of Zhengyi practice tracks ritual-legal correctness plus moral keeping of the oath. 6) Social conclusion: Community order mirrors celestial court order.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For BaZi remediation via Zhengyi-style petition: write clear ‘case file’—stem/branch affliction as charge, requested rectification as judgment sought. 2) Time audiences on days when the native’s useful god is strong and officer-star (official/7k) is not wildly hostile without support. 3) Maintain personal ‘covenant hygiene’: no petition while knowingly violating core precepts you already accepted. 4) Structure prayer as court document: title, identity, facts, request, closing formula—not emotional venting. 5) After rite, act in worldly law/ethics consistently; contradiction voids the symbolic contract.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Lingbao cosmogonic liturgies focused on universal salvation scripts, Zhengyi chaoyi is bureaucratic-legal. It differs from Shangqing’s visionary ascent (where the adept sees and merges) by emphasizing petition through office and oath. Compared with folk free-form prayer, it insists that form *is* the power channel.

entries.logic_thesis: The text proves that mortality crises, epidemics, and demonic harassment are administrative and stellar: the Northern Emperor and Seven Yuan control life-death registers, so unblocking, lamp-ritual, and invocation of the seven luminaries can rewrite misfortune at the level of cosmic registry, not only psychology.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Northern realm and Seven Yuan oversee ghosts and human lifespan books. 2) Premise: Calamity is often register-blockage or malefic stellar-demonic influence. 3) Inference: Aligning with Seven Yuan (recitation, lamps, talismans, memorials) petitions the competent court. 4) Inference: Multi-day focused practice concentrates intent enough to ‘move the register’. 5) Conclusion: Deliverance is jurisdictional appeal, not generic piety. 6) Cautionary conclusion: Only sincere, law-abiding appeal is honored; magic without virtue fails.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi: when chart shows heavy 七杀/羊刃/空亡 clusters with illness stars, consider Seven Yuan / Beidou-type timing rather than only five-element objects. 2) Lamp practice on days ruled by the afflicted planet/phase for that native. 3) Combine medical care with ritual—registry logic does not cancel physical cause. 4) Use 1×7 or 2×7 day intensive recitation windows when luck pillar enters clash. 5) Frame intent as ‘correct the book’, not hatred of enemies.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike general xiaomo (demon-dissolving) scriptures that stress wisdom-power of the adept, this text localizes authority in Beidi and Seven Yuan as officers of death-files. It differs from pure astrology by adding petitionary rite, and from pure exorcism by tying results to lifespan calculation (益算/解厄) rather than only expulsion.

entries.logic_thesis: Lingbao food-offering liturgy proves that postmortem suffering is partly hunger of unrefined qi, and that correctly empowered food, mantra, and mudra can convert that hunger into liberation. The argument is sacramental causality: ordinary food does not feed ghosts; transformed food does, because the rite changes the ontological status of the offering.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Wandering souls suffer lack—food, light, precepts, direction. 2) Premise: Lingbao methods can ‘open throat’, multiply food, and refine qi. 3) Inference: Without transformation mantras, offering remains human nutrition only. 4) Inference: Sequence (invite, purify, empower, distribute, dedicate, send) is the causal machine. 5) Conclusion: Compassion becomes effective when ritual technology matches the beings’ mode of existence. 6) Communal conclusion: Feeding the dead reorders the living community’s debt and fear.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Schedule施食 near death-anniversary stems/branches or Zhongyuan, checking that officiant’s chart can support water-fire balance that day. 2) Before offering, regulate breath and intention so ‘empowerment’ is not empty chant. 3) Name categories of beings (ancestors, lonely souls, disaster dead) to avoid vague magic. 4) Dedicate merit back to the living chart’s useful gods—close the loop. 5) Teach families that ethical amends in life reduce the ‘hunger’ their dead carry.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Buddhist Yankou, which is its sibling in form, Lingbao shishi embeds Daoist salvation ranks, talismans, and Heavenly Worthies as the conversion engine. It differs from Zhengyi court petitions (legal) by being alimentary-transformative, and from jilian neifa by remaining more liturgical-public than operator-alchemy centered.

entries.name_han: 历世真仙体道通鉴后编
entries.logic_thesis: The sequel-hagiography proves Dao by induction across history: successive verified biographies of embodied immortals show that ‘attaining Dao’ is a repeatable human possibility, not a mythic singularity. Its logic is evidentiary—pattern of lives, methods, and outcomes constitutes a collective proof stronger than any single claim.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: If Dao were unreal, consistent long-term cases of transformation would not accumulate. 2) Premise: Multiple eras and methods still converge on embodiment (体道). 3) Inference: Diversity of paths is compatible with unity of goal. 4) Inference: Failures and partial attainments in the record refine what counts as evidence. 5) Conclusion: Hagiography is a dataset for cultivating confidence and method selection. 6) Meta-conclusion: Later generations inherit a duty to continue the empirical-spiritual ledger.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When a BaZi shows strong ‘immortal’ patterns (clear output + resource + seal with stable structure), study matching historical cases rather than generic advice. 2) Extract method families from biographies (alchemy, ritual, virtue, hermit) and match to chart temperament. 3) Use ‘通鉴’ attitude: track your own practice years as data, not drama. 4) Avoid single-guru absolutism—the corpus itself is plural. 5) Treat moral biography (deeds) as seriously as technique chapters.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike doctrinal scriptures that argue from cosmology downward, this work argues from cases upward. It differs from pure genealogies of gods by focusing on human practitioners across dynasties, and from technical manuals by subordinating recipe detail to the narrative proof that embodiment happened.

entries.logic_thesis: This classic proves that all fortune, body, and practice outcomes are functions of yin-yang imbalance and five-phase generation/control cycles operating uniformly from cosmos to person. It establishes the shared algebraic grammar underlying medicine, alchemy, and fate calculation—without which BaZi would be superstition and cultivation would be random.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Dao differentiates as yin-yang. 2) Premise: Yin-yang further articulates as five phases with fixed generation and conquest relations. 3) Inference: Any concrete system (organs, seasons, stems, branches, medicines) is a mapping onto this algebra. 4) Inference: Diagnosis is locating excess/deficiency and blocked cycles. 5) Conclusion: Remedy is restoring dynamic balance, not maximizing one phase. 6) Universal conclusion: Taiqing purity is balanced five-phase circulation, not annihilation of yin.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Standard BaZi workflow: Day Master strength → useful god → taboo god, always justified in generation/control language. 2) For annual luck: check whether incoming pillar generates useful god or strengthens taboo. 3) Cultivation: time breathing/meditation to support deficient phases (e.g., more restorative practice in seasons that feed the weak phase). 4) Refuse one-sided ‘boost metal’ style fixes when control cycle will rebound. 5) Cross-check body symptoms with phase theory before spiritualizing problems.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with pure Yijing image-number, this text is more explicitly five-phase medical-alchemical. It differs from moral Daodejing readings by being operational cosmology, and from star-lore (Seven Yuan) by grounding causality in elemental relations rather than stellar officers.

entries.name_han: 黄帝太一八门逆顺生死诀
entries.logic_thesis: The text proves that life-death outcomes in movement, combat, and selection of time-space are governed by Taiyi’s eight gates running in reverse or forward according to yin-yang dun patterns. Correct alignment with gate-qi can convert a deadly configuration into a viable path; misalignment inverts luck even on a ‘good’ calendar day.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Taiyi cycles and eight gates (休生伤杜景死惊开) structure spatial-temporal luck. 2) Premise: Yang-dun and yin-dun reverse the running of stems vs gates. 3) Inference: ‘生/开/休’ gates favor life and entry; ‘死/伤/惊’ favor avoidance or attack under rule. 4) Inference: Formulae that place 戊 on 休 and run gates/stems correctly yield ‘immortal path not far’. 5) Conclusion: Survival strategy is navigational knowledge of reverse/forward gate-law. 6) Extension: The same logic applies to choosing dwellings, travel, and ritual timing.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When BaZi year/month is harsh, select event days where local 奇门/太乙 gate supporting the native’s useful god is open (生/开/休). 2) Avoid signing, surgery, or confrontation on personal 死/惊 gates unless the method specifically uses them. 3) For exorcistic or assertive rites, prefer gates that match intent (e.g., 伤 for cutting, 开 for initiating). 4) Learn yang-dun vs yin-dun half-year switch so you do not run formulae backward. 5) Integrate with BaZi: gate choice is tactical; chart structure is strategic.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike BaZi, which profiles a life’s phase economy from birth data, this text is operational time-space tactics under Taiyi. It differs from pure Liuren or standard Qimen manuals mainly in its explicit ‘逆顺生死’ framing and legendary military transmission, emphasizing survival polarity over general divination breadth.

entries.name_han: 上清太极隐注玉经宝诀
entries.logic_thesis: This Shangqing-Lingbao hybrid proves that scriptures are graded living forces: correct reception, collation, and recitation under oath determine whether texts heal and immortalize or inflict ‘wind-blade’ penalties. Transmission protocol is the safety lock on cosmic software; hidden annotations reveal that method without ritual legality backfires.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Jade scriptures are high-frequency true writs, not ordinary books. 2) Premise: Errors in characters, illicit transmission, or impure reception injure lifespan. 3) Inference: Collation thrice, pure covenants, and graded eligibility protect both parties. 4) Inference: Recitation of proper texts can offset karmic disease when done under ritual frame. 5) Conclusion: Spiritual literacy is regulated access to power, analogous to handling medicine. 6) Soteriological conclusion: Seeing this text marks predestined immortal office—if vows are kept.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat any advanced BaZi/Daoist formula set as ‘经’: document lineage of method, do not remix casually. 2) Before teaching a powerful remedial rite, require a period of purity and clear vows (no harm, no sale of fear). 3) When clients have chronic unexplained illness in chart, combine medical care with ordered scripture-recitation rather than random mantras. 4) Maintain textual hygiene—wrong strokes in talismans are the modern equivalent of wrong characters. 5) Prefer fewer authentic practices over many leaked fragments.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike public Daodejing prefaces that invite broad cultivation, this text restricts and weaponizes access. It differs from Zhengyi court codes by focusing on scripture-as-body and visionary Shangqing grades, and from pure morality precepts by making philological care (字校) itself a salvific discipline.

entries.logic_thesis: The scripture proves that advanced attainment recreates the embryonic state: by returning breath, spirit, and intention to the ‘womb’ of the body-cosmos, the adept restarts generation from the undivided, escaping the exhaustion of postnatal qi. Embryonic breathing is not metaphor alone but the causal reset of life-process.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Postnatal life leaks original qi through breath, emotion, and desire. 2) Premise: The fetus lives without ordinary panting, nourished by primordial unity. 3) Inference: Practices that close the mouth-nose dependence and interiorize breath reverse leakage. 4) Inference: When spirit rests in the lower/central ‘womb’, postnatal and prenatal reconnect. 5) Conclusion: Longevity and spiritual rebirth share one mechanism—embryonic return. 6) Warning: Forced breath-holding without guidance inverts the benefit.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For BaZi charts with severe rootlessness or exhausted resource, prioritize soft embryonic breathing over intense cathartic practices. 2) Practice after midnight or in quiet hours when postnatal stimulation is low. 3) Couple with moral quietude—anger and lust are anti-embryonic. 4) Use seasonal ‘storage’ months to deepen, not to push extremes. 5) Track pulse, sleep, and emotional reactivity as indicators of true return vs repression.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with general qi-absorption methods, Baotai Jing specifies the fetal model as the gold standard of breath. It differs from sexual-alchemy dual cultivation by being primarily solitary-interior, and from waidan by locating the womb of rebirth in the practitioner’s own psychosomatic field.

entries.logic_thesis: This text proves that ‘demons’ are both external pathogens and internal afflictive forces, and that they dissolve under clarified wisdom-power and correct recitation rather than under mere violence. The core argument: obstruction is removable because it lacks ultimate root in Dao; illumination cancels it.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Demonic interference thrives on fear, turbidity, and ignorance. 2) Premise: Dao’s true writ carries clarifying force (消). 3) Inference: Recitation plus upright mind removes fuel demons need. 4) Inference: Internal demons (三尸-type passions) and external specters share a vulnerability to clarity. 5) Conclusion: Exorcism without self-purification is incomplete; self-purification is already half exorcism. 6) Pastoral conclusion: Teach courage and clarity as primary talismans.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When BaZi shows heavy sha and illness with panic symptoms, combine boundary-setting rites with cognitive-clarity practice (name the fear precisely). 2) Daily short recitation aimed at ‘dissolving turbidity’, not cursing enemies. 3) Clean sleep, diet, and media inputs—turbid lifestyle feeds ‘魔’. 4) Use days when seal/resource stars support the native for formal 消魔 work. 5) Evaluate success by reduced compulsion and clearer decisions, not only omens.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Seven Yuan / Beidi texts that appeal to stellar-northern jurisdiction, Xiaomo Jing emphasizes the dissolving power of revealed wisdom itself. It differs from purely medical pathogen theory by retaining moral-spiritual agency, and from jilian by targeting affliction of the living more than salvation of the dead.

entries.logic_thesis: The scripture proves lifespan is numerically administered (‘算’) and can be increased through alliance with Xiwangmu’s life-bestowing authority when the petitioner meets moral and ritual conditions. It establishes that years are not only biological residue but adjustable allotment under divine accounting.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Each person has a lifespan count overseen by celestial offices, with Xiwangmu as a paramount life-nourishing figure. 2) Premise: Misdeeds and ritual neglect shorten count; virtue and proper petition can restore or add. 3) Inference: ‘益算’ rites are accounting corrections, not defiance of Dao. 4) Inference: Efficacy requires sincerity, purity, and correct timing/invocation. 5) Conclusion: Longevity practice includes ethical capital plus formal appeal to the life-giver. 6) Limit: Gains without reformed conduct are unstable.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, when life-palace and health stars are weak but resources can be cultivated, use 益算 framing for long-horizon lifestyle reform, not panic magic. 2) Birthday or renri rites dedicated to life-extension with concrete vows (quit a vice, serve parents). 3) Pair with medical checkups—算 includes body maintenance. 4) Prefer generating-cycle years for major life-extension retreats. 5) Record baseline health metrics; ‘added years’ should appear as added resilience.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with general Beidou destiny scriptures, this text privileges Xiwangmu as the life-augmenting pole. It differs from pure neidan longevity (which stores essence) by stressing petitionary increase of the register, and from fatalistic BaZi readings by asserting lawful plasticity of the lifespan number.

entries.logic_thesis: Building on Laozi’s ‘Valley Spirit does not die’, this work proves that immortality is the continuous functioning of empty, receptive, generative capacity (玄牝) rather than accumulation of force. The valley is not weak; its emptiness is the indestructible root that births heaven-earth in the body.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: What is full breaks; what is empty can receive without end. 2) Premise: The ‘valley spirit’ names the undying generative emptiness (玄牝之门). 3) Inference: Cultivation that fills the mind with striving kills the valley; yielding preserves it. 4) Inference: Soft continuous use (‘绵绵若存’) outperforms violent effort. 5) Conclusion: True yang is born from protected emptiness, not from aggressive yang-forcing. 6) Neidan conclusion: Guard the mysterious female gate as the practical root of returned elixir.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For charts overloaded with output and officer (busy, drained types): prescribe valley practice—more silence, less performing. 2) Meditation: rest attention in lower belly/empty center without squeezing breath. 3) Speech discipline: reduce unnecessary words as ‘not exhausting the valley’. 4) In yearly luck of extreme fire/wood arousal, deliberately schedule emptiness days. 5) Judge practice by spontaneous stability and less craving, not by dramatic qi sensations.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike furnace-heavy neidan tracts, Gushen Pian keeps Laozi’s emptiness as the master key. It differs from precept texts (external restraint) by offering an ontological image for why restraint works, and from five-phase engineering texts by prioritizing one metaphor—the living valley—over multi-organ taxonomy.

entries.logic_thesis: This treatise proves returned-elixir attainment by a chorus of immortal authorities: when many realized figures converge on the same alchemical logic, the method is validated beyond private opinion. The argument is consensus-of-the-realized plus technical unity—many voices, one dan-path.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Isolated claims of immortality are epistemically weak. 2) Premise: Multiple immortals articulate compatible stages of lead-mercury / yin-yang return. 3) Inference: Convergence indicates structure of reality, not sect fashion. 4) Inference: Divergent outer images still point to one reverse-flow of essence-qi-spirit. 5) Conclusion: Study should extract the shared skeleton, discard ornamental contradictions. 6) Practical conclusion: Choose a coherent lineage thread and complete it, using the ‘众仙’ as cross-check.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When reading many masters confuses a student, force a one-page synthesis of shared stages (stop leak → gather → cook → return → stabilize). 2) Match stage emphasis to BaZi: leaky charts start at sealing; stagnant charts at gentle movement. 3) Use biographies inside the text as pacing models—years, not weeks. 4) Reject any modern promise that skips the shared skeleton. 5) Quarterly review: which stage am I actually in, evidenced by life conduct?
entries.logic_compare: Unlike single-author neidan revelations, this work’s authority is anthological. It differs from hagiography (体道通鉴) by focusing on method-arguments rather than life stories alone, and from purely laboratory waidan by reading ‘returned cinnabar’ primarily as internal reversion illustrated through immortal discourse.

entries.logic_thesis: Mu Changchao proves that the proliferation of teachings, rites, and phenomena all issue from and return to one mysterious source (玄/元始三炁); therefore sectarian multiplicity is pedagogic, not ultimate. Direct pointing means collapsing ten thousand methods into their single root without nihilism—forms remain useful until return is complete.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Yuanqi differentiates into heaven-earth, three lights, five phases, eight trigrams, humans. 2) Premise: All later dharmas are elaborations of that differentiation. 3) Inference: Clinging to branch methods as absolute multiplies delusion. 4) Inference: Yet denying methods before realizing the root is also error. 5) Conclusion: True mastery uses methods as fingers, then rests in the moon of unified return. 6) Pedagogical conclusion: ‘直指’ is ruthlessly simple orientation amid Daoist scholastic complexity.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For advanced students drowning in techniques: inventory all practices → map each to a root function (quiet, circulate, refine, save beings) → cut redundancies. 2) BaZi counseling: many remedial gadgets → one structural useful-god strategy. 3) Daily: begin and end with a minute of returning attention to source-breath before any complex method. 4) Interfaith/inter-sect reading: translate foreign terms into your root model rather than collecting exoticisms. 5) Success: fewer practices, deeper consistency.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with early revealed scriptures that multiply heavens and names, this Yuan-Ming synthesis recenters unity. It differs from Chan-style ‘direct pointing’ by keeping Daoist cosmogony (三炁) as the explicit ground, and from purely practical neidan by philosophically justifying why all methods can be collapsed.

entries.logic_thesis: Sectional exegesis proves that the Daodejing’s power is unlocked only when each pericope is decoded into concrete cultivation or cosmic correspondences rather than left as vague wisdom. The argument: structure of the text is instructional sequence; cutting and explaining sections reveals operative steps hidden in plain language.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Classic speech is compressed and polyvalent. 2) Premise: Without sectional keys, readers moralize or aestheticize without transformation. 3) Inference: Dividing the text into units allows mapping to body, state, and practice. 4) Inference: Early esoteric readings treat political language as inner governance. 5) Conclusion: Correct commentary is a causal interface between scripture and embodiment. 6) Critical conclusion: Commentary must serve practice verification, not literary display.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Study one short section per week; extract one behavioral experiment (e.g., ‘不争’ in a real conflict). 2) Link sections to BaZi themes: humility sections for strong officer charts; contentment for wealth-heavy charts. 3) Keep a dual column: ‘surface meaning’ vs ‘body-state meaning’. 4) Recite only after sectional understanding to avoid empty chanting. 5) Discard interpretations that cannot change a measurable habit in 30 days.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike the Xujue, which sacralizes the whole text’s ontology, Jie Jie works microscopically on segments. It differs from Heshanggong’s systematic longevity allegory mainly in form (sectional cuts) and from pure philology by insisting that the cut exists for praxis, not for academic completeness alone.

entries.logic_thesis: The Lingqi system proves that a simplified, castable image-set can carry Yijing-class decision guidance for ordinary people: because the cosmos’s pattern is ubiquitous, twelve spirit-tokens can sample it when ritual sincerity is present. Accessibility does not cancel depth; it democratizes pattern-reading under constraint of proper making and invocation.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Zhouyi is true but hard for daily use. 2) Premise: Sages may encode the same order in alternative lots (chess-like tokens). 3) Inference: Structured random cast + fixed oracle text yields actionable hexagram-like counsel. 4) Inference: Consecrated implements and prayer align the cast with the questioner’s qi field. 5) Conclusion: Divination works as patterned sampling of a lawful cosmos, not as chaos or fraud. 6) Ethical conclusion: Ask only proper questions; the tool amplifies clarity or confusion already present.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Use Lingqi when BaZi shows a fork (two plausible useful-god strategies) and a timely decision is needed. 2) Cast after stating one precise question; refuse multi-question noise. 3) Interpret oracle lines through the querent’s chart language (phases, official/wealth) for integration. 4) Prefer days when the querent’s seal/resource is not crushed—clarity needs support. 5) Archive casts vs outcomes to calibrate personal accuracy and humility.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike full Yijing professional yarrow practice, Lingqi is deliberately portable and popular. It differs from Taiyi Eight Gates (time-space tactics for movement/war) by being textual-oracular counsel for civil decisions, and from pure spirit-medium possession by using fixed classical responses rather than open channeling.

entries.logic_thesis: The collected precepts prove that graded moral-ritual restraints are the load-bearing structure of the Three Caverns path: without precepts, scriptures and techniques lack a vessel and turn destructive. Precepts are not lower than alchemy; they are the causal precondition that makes higher methods non-lethal to self and community.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Three Caverns transmit escalating sacred powers. 2) Premise: Power without restraint multiplies harm (to body, ghosts, society). 3) Inference: Ordination stages bind the adept to corresponding 戒. 4) Inference: Keeping precepts purifies the vessel so qi and spirit can stably rise. 5) Conclusion: Ethical law is technical infrastructure of immortality, not mere social etiquette. 6) Communal conclusion: Shared precepts create a trustworthy field for collective rites.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Before advanced BaZi remediation or ritual work, adopt a minimal personal code (no fraud, no sexual exploitation of clients, no fear-selling). 2) Match precept intensity to method intensity—stronger talismanic work, stricter purity windows. 3) Use confession/repair when broken: precept logic includes restoration, not only perfection. 4) In yearly luck of peer/rob-wealth stress, double down on non-greed precepts. 5) Teach students precepts as success conditions for practice, not as optional piety.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure wisdom texts that dissolve rules after awakening, Sandong precept literature insists rules remain the chassis of transmission. It differs from single-lineage house rules by claiming pan-cavern scope, and from purely civil Confucian ethics by tying each restraint to liturgical eligibility and cosmic consequence.
